current.text: Smart joined the Rockets this offseason. Houston's guard rotation is crowded with Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Reed Sheppard and Bogdan Bogdanovic.
He is not in the projected starting five of VanVleet, Thompson, Durant, Smith and Sengun.
A note from 2026-10-12 says Smart has also started and outplayed Reed Sheppard.
Smart may lead the Houston bench in minutes. Ime Udoka coached him in Boston and values defense.
Experts expect Smart, together with Thompson and VanVleet, to take most of the point guard minutes ahead of Reed Sheppard.
He could become a streamer or an add when VanVleet sits.
With our March 28 end date, Houston plays a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is predicted to win 54 games. The team is expected to play it safe in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: Smart gives his value in assists and steals and does not score much.
He is not a traditional point guard, but he can bring the ball up and run the offense. He takes good care of the ball.
He is still a very good defender.
His shooting is a weak point. He is willing to shoot, but his FG% is low for a guard.

note: Smart is ranked 224 on Yahoo and 248 on ESPN, and both sites value him at 0 USD. That puts him well outside the 144 players drafted in our league, so do not draft him. His projected line has a weak FG% (39.6%), only 8.5 points and few rebounds, which leaves him a bench minutes player with steals, some threes and low turnovers. Early in the season, watch how many bench minutes Udoka gives him and pick him up on waivers when VanVleet misses games. His team's 10-game playoff schedule makes him less useful late in the season.
